Same host as before, so atom 13 is the cyclopentane CH bonded to the amide nitrogen at atom 11 - the anchor that leaves the azine free. I am building a two-dimensional picture of what C4 wants, along size and polarisability on one axis and electron withdrawal on the other. So far: methylthio is large, polarisable and donating; a methyl ketone is extended, polar and withdrawing; iodine is the largest and most polarisable with the weakest withdrawal. A trifluoromethyl fills the remaining corner - comparable in bulk to a bromine or an isopropyl, strongly withdrawing through induction, and essentially non-polarisable, since fluorine holds its electrons tightly. Bromine at 0.60 and the nitrile at 0.58 are the two best groups so far and they disagree on electronics, so this corner is the one that decides it: if trifluoromethyl scores with them, withdrawal is what matters and polarisability is a coincidence. It will cost QED - about 322 Da at LogP near 4.6 - so this is a characterisation call rather than a contender. Cyclopentyl cap again, which is activity-neutral.
